title: Crossing
description: A summer photograph of a Japanese level crossing, seen from below and looking up past the crossbuck into the sky, that turns out to be built like a paper tunnel book, seen through a window cut in the page. Drag, or tilt your phone, and it comes apart behind that window into its real depth planes: the sky card stands back, the wires hang in the middle, the crossbuck and its lamps float forward, each a cut-out with the street continued behind it, throwing soft shadows on the cards behind. The lens focuses on whichever plane is under your finger. Let go and it closes back into one flat photograph.
intent: Multiple layers of an image, the physical world inside the computer. After Disney's multiplane camera (1937, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multiplane_camera) and paper tunnel books (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunnel_book): one low-angle photo cut offline into seven matted, inpainted planes that separate in z with true perspective, each scaled so that from the lens axis the stack is still exactly the photograph.

sources.author: PJH (@dokae)
sources.note: Ukyo, Kyoto; 4928x3264 original (Ricoh GR II). Plated from the curated low-angle library frame kyoto-crossing-lowangle (4000x2649; chosen over setagaya-wires-up as the steeper, about 35 degrees up, and more cobalt frame). Depth from Depth Anything V2 Small via tools/depth/depth_hr.py; planes, mattes and inpainting baked by tools/depth/bakes/crossing (labels.py, bake.py): the sky card filled from a dilated matte and outpainted a quarter past each side, every wire refitted as one catenary by wires.py and rehung by catenary.py in three gauges and a hairline, each with its own ink and sag, thinning and taking the sky's colour as it runs off under the eave, two of the five that crossed the cumulus taken down (the closed photograph is the stack itself, so the wires are in it from the first frame), running on under the old house far past the frame and behind the signal so no wire ends in open sky, the barrier boom's orange and red band regraded to a muted ochre and a dull brick (boomgrade.py) so the crossbuck is the one warm accent, hidden house and town texture and the town card's overscan margin by LaMa (tools/depth/fill.py), the town card's top keyed clean of the photo's old sky and ended on its ridge tiles, with what the signal hides there refilled from the town alone (townmatte.py), the signal lamps' bristly keyed rims opened, pulled in a px and a half and feathered (lamphood.py), every card that meets the frame overscanned so the front mat never shows an edge.

sources.author: W.carter (Wikimedia Commons)
sources.note: The cumulus behind the street: a dense cumulus congestus, hard cauliflower-edged sunlit towers over solid shaded flanks, filling its frame (it replaces the side-lit mediocris of Poly Haven's kloofendal_48d_partly_cloudy_puresky, a thin, broken cloud that every relight left a mottled veil). Mirrored so its sun stands up and to the right, as in the photo; keyed from its clear blue sky (whiter, brighter or darker than the sky filled in under it), every pocket inside its silhouette made cloud so no sky shows through the mass; carried on past the photo's left and bottom edges far behind the old house and the town; its left flank, where the photo cuts the dark foreground cloud off, cut back and rebuilt as round shaded billows that drop in behind the eave, and its right side under the crown as bigger lit lobes stepping in toward the base; its own luminance mapped onto the cloud ramp (skylight blues #7f9bbd to #bacbde in the shade, warm near-white #f4f1ea on the lit towers) with each lobe's local contrast raised so the crevices fall into shade; and placed so it rises from behind the far roofs and the left eave past the crossbuck's arms into the top third of the sky, by tools/depth/bakes/crossing/cumulus.py, on a card of its own between the sky and the far houses, feathered to nothing well inside its edges. Then tools/depth/bakes/crossing/cloudlight.py makes the card one solid mass (soft edges rebuilt as lobes, only the outer rim feathered, the lower body's lobes a little firmer over skylight-blue cores) and lays a soft warm-neutral glow over the crown's sunward lobes that rolls off at #f4f1ea, never a flat white. The photo's own torn cloud wisps are gone from the sky card, which is now the clear gradient alone.
